statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). Tail 21% (watch), Stress 46% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail sits in the watch band and below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH. The reason for the step up from the overnight 12-13 band is specific and observed: the U.S. cash open was bought, the Nasdaq-100 is holding the upper third of its cash range, NQ futures sit within 19 points of the session high, the semiconductor index is near its own high, and the VIX is at a session low while 2Y, 5Y and 10Y yields and both crude benchmarks are lower. That is post-open continuation inside an aligned risk-on regime. It stops short of the block band because only one directional leg has been observed, the advance is a fifth the size of Monday's, and the open-hour dip to 30,496.43 was a genuine two-way test. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 14:00-16:00 UTC band covering the Jefferson remarks and the resolution of the opening drive, which is published as the danger window instead of the whole session. Secondary checkpoints sit at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction with Barkin, and in the 19:00 UTC power hour that carried Monday's highest Tail reading. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping. The reading would move into the block band on a shallow rejection of the 30,679.98 cash high that is immediately bought, repeated extension after failed retracements, or the index holding a session extreme while yields, VIX, oil, semiconductors and breadth all confirm one direction.
headline: The U.S. cash open was bought and the Nasdaq-100 holds the upper third of its range with NQ 19 points under the session high, semiconductors and a 14.43 VIX session low aligned behind it; observed post-open continuation lifts Tail to the watch band while a contractionary Richmond Fed print pushes yields lower
body: Monday closed with the Nasdaq-100 cash index at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83%, as an AI and semiconductor rally lifted the Nasdaq Composite 2.26% to a record 27,122.09, with AMD up about 10% to become the fourth U.S. chipmaker worth $1 trillion, Intel up about 12%, Qualcomm more than 9% and Meta about 11% on the reception of its Muse AI assistant. The 13:30 UTC cash open, which was not observable in the delayed feeds available at the previous assessment, is now observable and it changes the reading. What is observed. The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,650.50 to 30,652.50, up 0.55-0.56%, inside a 30,496.43-30,679.98 cash range confirmed identically by two independent quote sources. The open was sold down to 30,496.43, only 14 points above Monday's close, and that dip was bought; the index then rallied 183 points to 30,679.98 and now sits about 28 points under that high, in the upper third of the range. NQ Dec-26 futures trade at 30,964.75 to 30,967.00, up 0.58-0.59% against a 30,784.75 settlement, inside a 30,670.00-30,983.75 range, which places the contract within roughly 19 points of its session high. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is 12,559.80, up 1.02%, and is likewise near its 12,560.22 session high. This is post-open continuation with the index and its leadership group both holding close to a session extreme, and it is the reason Tail moves up from the 12-13 overnight band. What holds Tail inside the watch band rather than the block band. Only one directional leg has been observed since the open. There is no sequence of failed retracements, no repeated extension, and the dip into 30,496.43 was a genuine two-way test that resolved through the range rather than a shallow refusal to retrace. The advance itself is modest at 0.56%, roughly a fifth of Monday's move, and the 183-point cash range over the first hour is not a runaway. Monday's much larger trend day carried published Tail readings of 26 to 33 across the equivalent hours; today's structure does not yet support that. Cross-asset evidence is aligned, but the alignment is disinflationary rather than the tightening kind that normally accompanies a pathological one-way path. The VIX is 14.43, down 2.96% from a 14.87 close and sitting at its 14.43 session low inside a 14.43-14.95 band. The 2-year yield is 4.75% and the 5-year 4.83%, each about 0.6 basis points lower, the 10-year 4.95% and about 2 basis points lower, with the 30-year fractionally higher at 5.29%. WTI is $90.86, down 1.63%, and Brent $99.56, down 0.77%, a fifth consecutive lower session. Falling yields and falling crude remove the tightening channel that usually accompanies a lethal trend leg, which is why this alignment is treated as supportive of an orderly grind rather than as a Tail amplifier in its own right. Scheduled evidence verified this run. The Richmond Fed's Fifth District manufacturing composite printed -2 for September against a +5 forecast and +4 previous, with shipments at -5 from +11, new orders at -6 from +3, local business conditions at -6 from +4 and employment the only improving component at +7 from -2. This was confirmed at the Richmond Fed's own survey page and in independent reporting. A contractionary regional survey is consistent with the lower yields observed alongside it. Williams spoke at 14:05 UTC and Jefferson at 14:20 UTC; both fall inside the current clock hour and inside the published danger window. The next scheduled checkpoint is the 17:00 UTC 2-year note auction alongside Barkin. Geopolitics and policy remain two-sided and unresolved. Reporting confirms an Iranian offer, delivered through mediators, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade; Washington has not publicly accepted those conditions, so this is a live headline risk in both directions and part of the reason crude is falling. A Trump-Xi summit is confirmed for Thursday in Washington, but no exact time could be verified, so it is deliberately omitted from the structured event list rather than published with a guessed timestamp and is carried instead as a checkpoint in the hourly drivers. Two source-hygiene notes. The aggregated economic calendar consulted for this run again displayed populated actual values for releases still days in the future, which is a parsing artefact of its previous-period column; no future release outcome from that table has been treated as verified or published as news, and only the Richmond Fed print, independently confirmed at the primary source, is published in the hourly news fields as a released outcome. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was not used as evidence: its payload is timestamped 10:23 UTC against a 90-minute freshness bar, its collection status is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are both unavailable, so this assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources. The dominant mode is trend-up. Stress at 46 reflects the record-high starting point, narrow AI and semiconductor leadership, the contractionary regional survey, the clustered Fed speaker block now passing, the pending 2-year auction and the unresolved Hormuz thread. Confidence at 88 reflects current verified levels for the cash index and futures from two independent sources each, the volatility index, the semiconductor index, four Treasury points and both crude benchmarks, plus a primary-source macro release and a cross-checked seven-day calendar; the deduction is that tick-level pullback depth within the opening hour is not directly observable and no independent cross-asset context was available to corroborate.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments, none of them revised with later information. Tail built through Monday's U.S. session as the index trended to a record close, peaking at 33 with Stress 57 in the 19:00 UTC hour; every hour from 14:00 to 19:00 UTC mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. After the cash close the trend-up characterisation gave way to a normal two-way regime: Tail fell to 23 by 20:00 UTC and 14 by 21:00 UTC, then held an 11-13 band for the entire Asian and European overnight with Stress between 32 and 39 and Confidence between 85 and 87. Every hour from 21:00 UTC onward mapped to EA_ON. The final lookback hour, 13:00 UTC, carried Tail 13 with Stress 43 and Confidence 84, the lower Confidence reflecting that the cash open had not yet become observable in the delayed feeds available at that time.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside a 11-23 band. The six U.S. cash hours from 14:00 to 19:00 UTC sit in the watch band and map to WATCH, peaking at 23 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, the same hour that carried Monday's highest reading. From the 20:00 UTC cash close the path assumes liquidity drains and the directional characterisation loses definition: Tail falls to 17, then 14, then settles onto an 11-13 overnight floor that mirrors the band actually observed through the previous night. It rebuilds gradually from the 07:00 UTC European open and reaches 17 in the final hour, which contains both Wednesday's cash open at 13:30 UTC and the high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC. Stress peaks at 48 in the power hour and again at 46 in that final PMI hour. No forecast hour reaches the block threshold, because pre-event alignment is not scored as observed structure and no post-release price path is observable from this cutoff. Confidence decays from 88 to 66 across the window for the same reason.
